title: Playing with Spanish articles
summary: Practise Spanish articles and how they agree with nouns.
keyIdeas: Articles go with nouns: el perro, la mesa, los libros, las flores.
Spanish has definite articles (el, la, los, las) and indefinite articles (un, una, unos, unas).
An article agrees with the noun's gender and number. There are special cases such as 'el agua', which is feminine.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas la producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: In «el perro», the article goes with a masculine singular noun.
activities.explanation: Use «el» in «el lápiz» and «el perro» because these nouns are masculine and singular.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence with the correct article.
activities.explanation: Use «los» because «libros» is masculine and plural.
activities.sentence: Hugo guarda ___ libros nuevos en la mochila.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish articles by number.
activities.explanation: Singular articles go with nouns naming one thing or being. Plural articles go with nouns naming more than one.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish article to the noun it fits.
activities.explanation: Each article must agree with the noun's gender and number.

activities.prompt: Omar is in art class. Which Spanish question uses the correct article?
activities.explanation: Use «unas ceras» because «ceras» is feminine and plural.

activities.prompt: Find the Spanish sentence with an incorrect article.
activities.explanation: «la cuadernos» is incorrect because «cuadernos» is masculine and plural. Use «los cuadernos».

activities.prompt: Choose the correct Spanish indefinite article.
activities.explanation: Use «una» because «mariposa» is feminine and singular.
activities.sentence: En el jardín vimos ___ mariposa de colores.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish text carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The text has definite articles such as «el» and «las», and indefinite articles such as «unos» and «una».
activities.title: El huerto escolar
activities.text: Hoy visitamos el huerto. Hugo riega las plantas verdes. Aisha coge unos tomates rojos. En el suelo hay una regadera grande. Todos cuidamos las flores con cariño.

questions.prompt: Which article goes with «tomates» in the text?
questions.explanation: The text says, «Aisha coge unos tomates rojos».
«plantas» is feminine and plural, so it needs «las».
options: Because it is feminine and plural.
Because it is masculine and singular.
Because it names just one thing.

activities.prompt: Put the Spanish sentence in order: who sings, then the action, then where.
activities.explanation: The sentence starts with a capital letter in «Los» and ends with the full stop in «árbol.».
